reasons: Large file with many parts and no tests visible in the packet.
The cookie is written here but not read in this file.
A comment in the file says the rail cursor does not fully work with Tailwind 3.4.

terms.meaning: a way for components to share data without passing it down through every level
a small saved note in the browser that the site can read later
a screen width at which the layout changes, such as switching to the desktop view

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and fixed sizes
sections.what: Brings in the parts this sidebar uses and sets its fixed sizes, cookie name, cookie lifetime and shortcut letter.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping sizes and names in one place so they change together.
sections.watch_out: The cookie name must stay the same wherever it is read, or saved state is lost.

sections.name: SidebarContextProps
sections.title: Shape of shared sidebar data
sections.what: Describes the data shared with every sidebar part: expanded or collapsed state, open flags, toggle functions and whether the screen is a phone.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed shape keeps every part reading the same names.
sections.watch_out: A new field must also be added to the provider's value, or parts will receive undefined.

sections.name: useSidebar
sections.title: Hook that reads sidebar state
sections.what: Lets a sidebar part read the shared state and throws a clear error if it is used outside the provider.
sections.why: Likely reason: the error catches a common mistake early.
sections.watch_out: Every sidebar part must sit inside SidebarProvider, or the page will crash.

sections.name: SidebarProvider (part 1)
sections.title: Open state and keyboard shortcut
sections.what: Keeps track of whether the sidebar is open, lets a parent control it, saves desktop state in a cookie, and toggles it on Ctrl or Cmd plus b.
sections.why: Likely reason: state lives in one place so all sidebar parts stay in step.
sections.watch_out: The keyboard listener is on the whole window, so it can fire while the user types in other fields.

sections.name: SidebarProvider (part 2)
sections.title: Shared state and page layout
sections.what: Packages the state for the shared context and wraps the children in a tooltip provider and a wrapper that sets the sidebar width values.
sections.why: Likely reason: tooltips for collapsed icons need a provider, and the width values let the CSS adjust the layout.
sections.watch_out: The tooltip delay is set to zero, so tooltips appear instantly on hover.

sections.name: Sidebar (part 1)
sections.title: Fixed and phone versions
sections.what: Returns a plain fixed column when collapsible is none, and a slide-in drawer on phones.
sections.why: Likely reason: phones cannot fit a full sidebar, so the drawer uses the sheet component.
sections.watch_out: The phone drawer hides the default close button and uses a screen-reader-only title.

sections.name: Sidebar (part 2)
sections.title: Desktop sidebar layout
sections.what: Builds the desktop sidebar with a spacer that holds the width and a fixed container that slides or narrows, depending on variant and collapse mode.
sections.why: Likely reason: the spacer keeps page content from sliding under the sidebar.
sections.watch_out: The layout depends on data attributes on the outer div, so removing them breaks the collapse animation.

sections.name: SidebarTrigger
sections.title: Button that toggles the sidebar
sections.what: A small icon button that opens or closes the sidebar when clicked, and still runs any click handler the parent supplied.
sections.why: Likely reason: a toggle near the page header is a common, expected place.
sections.watch_out: The parent's click handler runs before the toggle, so anything it does happens first.

sections.name: SidebarRail
sections.title: Thin edge strip for toggling
sections.what: An edge strip along the side of the sidebar that toggles it when clicked and shows a resize-style cursor.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets users click the edge to open or close, a pattern common in editors.
sections.watch_out: A comment in the file says some cursor selectors do not work in this Tailwind version, so the cursor may not change.

sections.name: SidebarInset
sections.title: Main content area beside the sidebar
sections.what: Creates the main page area that fills the space next to the sidebar, with rounded and shadowed styling in inset mode.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps page content in the right place beside the sidebar.
sections.watch_out: The inset styling only applies when the sidebar variant is inset; other variants look plain.

sections.name: SidebarInput
sections.title: Input box styled for the sidebar
sections.what: A short input field styled to fit inside the sidebar.
sections.why: Likely reason: reuses the standard input with a smaller, lighter look.
sections.watch_out: It relies on the shared input component, so changes there also change this.

sections.name: SidebarHeader
sections.title: Top area of the sidebar
sections.what: A column at the top of the sidebar for a logo or title, with padding and spacing.
sections.why: Likely reason: consistent padding for the top area.
sections.watch_out: Nothing is enforced; anything placed here is simply stacked.

sections.name: SidebarFooter
sections.title: Bottom area of the sidebar
sections.what: The same layout as the header, placed at the bottom, for things like a user menu.
sections.why: Likely reason: matching structure gives a consistent look.
sections.watch_out: This is only a container; the parent must place it at the bottom.

sections.name: SidebarSeparator
sections.title: Divider line in the sidebar
sections.what: A thin line that separates sidebar sections, using the sidebar's own border colour.
sections.why: Likely reason: a themed line matches the sidebar colours.
sections.watch_out: It inherits the shared separator's behaviour, so it needs a size from the parent in some layouts.

sections.name: SidebarContent
sections.title: Scrollable middle area
sections.what: The main body of the sidebar. It scrolls when items overflow and hides overflow when shrunk to icons.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the menu reachable on short screens.
sections.watch_out: Overflow is hidden in icon mode, so labels cut off there cannot be scrolled to.

sections.name: SidebarGroup
sections.title: Section grouping items
sections.what: A padded block that groups related menu items together.
sections.why: Likely reason: a simple container for labelled sections.
sections.watch_out: It is only a container; spacing and labels come from its child parts.

sections.name: SidebarGroupLabel
sections.title: Small heading for a group
sections.what: A small faded heading above a group. In icon mode it slides up and fades out.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps headings out of the way when only icons show.
sections.watch_out: The asChild option swaps the element, so the child's behaviour and styling take over.

sections.name: SidebarGroupAction
sections.title: Small action button on a group heading
sections.what: A small square button in the top right of a group, such as an add button. It is hidden in icon mode.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a group carry an action without an extra row.
sections.watch_out: It is positioned absolutely, so it can overlap a long group label.

sections.name: SidebarGroupContent
sections.title: Body of a group
sections.what: Wraps the items inside a group with full width and small text.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps text size consistent for group items.
sections.watch_out: It only sets styling; no behaviour is attached.

sections.name: SidebarMenu
sections.title: List container for menu items
sections.what: A column list that holds the menu items with small gaps.
sections.why: Likely reason: using a list element gives correct meaning for a menu.
sections.watch_out: Items must go inside list items; other markup breaks the list structure.

sections.name: SidebarMenuItem
sections.title: Single menu row and its button styles
sections.what: Wraps one menu row and defines the button look, with variants for normal and outlined styles and sizes for small, default and large.
sections.why: Likely reason: separate variants let one button look different for selected or outlined states.
sections.watch_out: Only the listed variant and size names produce a style; other names give no style.

sections.name: SidebarMenuButton
sections.title: Clickable menu item with tooltip
sections.what: The main clickable entry in the menu. It can show a tooltip with its name when the sidebar is collapsed on desktop.
sections.why: Likely reason: in icon mode the names are hidden, so the tooltip keeps them readable.
sections.watch_out: The tooltip only shows on desktop when collapsed; it stays hidden on phones and when the sidebar is open.

sections.name: SidebarMenuAction
sections.title: Small action button on a menu row
sections.what: A small square button on the right of a menu row, such as a more-options menu. It can show only on hover.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps rows tidy until the user points at them.
sections.watch_out: In hover-only mode the button is hidden on desktop until hover, but phones always show it.

sections.name: SidebarMenuBadge
sections.title: Small count label on a menu row
sections.what: A small pill on the right of a row, such as a count of new items. It is hidden in icon mode.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows a number without taking space from the label.
sections.watch_out: The badge sits over the right edge of the row, so a long label can run under it.

sections.name: SidebarMenuSkeleton
sections.title: Loading placeholder for menu rows
sections.what: A grey loading bar, optionally with an icon placeholder, shown while menu items load.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows the layout while data loads so the page does not jump.
sections.watch_out: Its width is picked at random between 50 and 90 percent once per placeholder, so widths differ between placeholders.

sections.name: SidebarMenuSub
sections.title: Indented list for sub-items
sections.what: A nested list with a left line and indent for items under a menu entry. It is hidden in icon mode.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows the hierarchy visually.
sections.watch_out: Sub-items are hidden when the sidebar is collapsed to icons, so they cannot be reached in that state.

sections.name: SidebarMenuSubItem
sections.title: Single sub-item row
sections.what: Wraps one row inside the nested list.
sections.why: Likely reason: a standard list item for sub-menu structure.
sections.watch_out: Like the main list, it must sit inside the sub-list.

sections.name: SidebarMenuSubButton
sections.title: Clickable sub-menu link and exports
sections.what: A link-style row inside a nested menu, with small or medium text and an active highlight. It also lists all sidebar pieces for import.
sections.why: Likely reason: smaller text separates sub-items from main items.
sections.watch_out: It renders as a link element by default, so the parent must give it a real address or a handler to navigate.

summary: Builds the app's side navigation. It can expand, shrink to icons, hide off-screen, or become a slide-in drawer on phones.
purpose: Gives every page the same navigation sidebar that remembers whether it was open.
why: Likely reason: a shared shell lets every page reuse the same navigation layout and behaviour.
how: A provider holds the open or closed state and a mobile flag, and shares them through a context. On desktop the state is saved in a cookie. On phones the sidebar becomes a sheet. Desktop uses a spacer that holds the width plus a fixed container that slides or narrows. Smaller parts such as header, footer, menu, group and menu button style each section. Ctrl or Cmd plus b toggles the sidebar.
inputs: Default open state, controlled open state and its change handler, side, variant, collapse mode and children. The mobile check comes from a hook in another file.
outputs: A navigation column, a toggle button, and styled menu parts.
risks: The state is written to a cookie but this file never reads it on load, so the saved state only matters if the parent reads it. The cookie is set without extra security flags. The keyboard shortcut listens across the whole window, so it can fire while the user types elsewhere.
debug: If the sidebar will not toggle, check that the component is inside SidebarProvider, since useSidebar throws an error otherwise. If phones show the desktop layout, check the use-mobile hook. If the open state is not remembered, check whether the parent reads the sidebar_state cookie.
